**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Anchor the calendar migration to the release ancestry**

When this commit is passed to the guarded backend release command, `resolveReleaseContext` checks every `introducedBy` SHA with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`; `49ff02de...` is a sibling of `152f2c14...` (both have parent `2ce7a1a0...`), not its ancestor. Consequently, `node scripts/production-release.mjs plan --sha 152f2c14071b48512af94edb5332bacf3ce53eb9` aborts with “refusing to omit a registered migration,” so this calendar schema repair cannot be deployed through the required release lane.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Verified against the actual published PR heads: git merge-base --is-ancestor 49ff02de5ade1b8923f099c22af0bbf57350a078 HEAD exits 0. The normal history includes the schema introduction before manifest registration. The guarded release plan passes for the exact published head (444:9497be8f4;445:563dafa42), including all110 migrations. The temporary review commits cited here are not the release targets. No migration rewrite or squash is used; normal merge ancestry remains required. Actual plan output is retained locally for release preflight; this is planning, not deployment.
